# Threat model: Klarbefund, the iPhone app

The hub's threat model is [`threat-model.md`](/docs/security/threat-model-hub). This one is
for the app in `clients/ios`, which runs on a person's phone, holds their
laboratory values and sends nothing anywhere unless they say so. Written
2026-10-15 against commit `64737039`; each mitigation names the code or test
that shows it, and `clients/ios/Tests/SharedTests/SecurityPostureTests.swift`
pins the ones that are build settings. STRIDE, as in the hub's model.

## System context

```
   paper report ──camera──▶ ┌──────────────────────────────┐
   lab PDF ──files/share──▶ │ Klarbefund (iOS 26, Swift 6)  │
   Apple Health ──read───▶ │  OCR · coding · AES-GCM store │
                           └──────┬──────────┬────────────┘
                 optional, consent│          │optional, consent
                                  ▼          ▼
                 ┌──────────────────┐   ┌─────────────────────────┐
                 │ EHDS hub         │   │ explanation service      │
                 │ (ADR-049/054/057)│   │ on device by default;    │
                 │ OIDC+PKCE, App   │   │ hosted: Azure OpenAI EU  │
                 │ Attest, Bearer   │   │ data zone, or own key    │
                 └──────────────────┘   └─────────────────────────┘
```

Trust boundaries: the device (Secure Enclave, data protection, app sandbox)
is trusted as Apple provides it. Everything that leaves the device crosses a
boundary and does so only after a consent the person gave for that purpose.

## Assets

| Asset                                   | Where                                        | Why it matters                                         |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Laboratory values, reports, page images | the store, `ReportStore.swift`               | Art. 9 GDPR health data                                |
| The store key                           | Keychain, `WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly`       | decrypts everything above                              |
| Hub tokens (device grant, app token)    | Keychain, `ThisDeviceOnly`, `EHDSConnection` | write access to the person's own hub record            |
| App Attest key                          | Secure Enclave, `DeviceCheck`                | proves a genuine app to the hub when creating accounts |
| Consents and their history              | `Consents.swift`                             | the legal basis for every transfer                     |
| Diagnostics export                      | written on request only, ADR-038             | contains values; must never enter the repository       |

## STRIDE

### Spoofing

| Threat                                                    | Mitigation                                                                                                                           | Status |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------ |
| A fake app creates hub accounts or pushes data as the app | Account creation needs an Apple App Attest attestation the hub verifies (ADR-054); every later call carries the app token            | met    |
| A fake hub harvests tokens                                | OIDC discovery from the configured issuer only, PKCE S256, `ASWebAuthenticationSession`; ATS forbids plaintext (`OIDCSession.swift`) | met    |
| A fake explanation service reads values                   | The provider is named in the request the person approves (`CloudConsentSheet.swift`); HTTPS by ATS                                   | met    |
| Someone else at the unlocked phone                        | App lock: Face ID, Touch ID or the passcode before the cover lifts, on by default (`AppLock.swift`, ADR-060)                         | met    |

### Tampering

| Threat                                         | Mitigation                                                                                                            | Status   |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| Stored records altered on disk or over a cable | Each record AES-GCM sealed (authenticated), key in the Keychain; a cable test could not copy stored data              | met      |
| A misread value treated as a laboratory result | Provenance keeps OCR values `preliminary`; only a laboratory's own PDF text layer yields `final` (`Provenance.swift`) | met      |
| A tampered build                               | App Attest proves the app to the hub, not to itself; jailbreak and debugger detection declined with reasons (ADR-060) | accepted |
| A dependency with a backdoor                   | No third-party package at all (`Package.swift`, `project.yml`, `docs/sbom/klarbefund-ios.cdx.json`)                   | met      |

### Repudiation

| Threat                                | Mitigation                                                                                           | Status |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| "I never consented to that transfer"  | Consent events with time, holder and effective date, revocable, with history (`Consents.swift`)      | met    |
| What was sent cannot be reconstructed | A sync is a FHIR Bundle with a SHA-256 fingerprint the app records (`EHDSConnection.swift`, ADR-057) | met    |

### Information disclosure

| Threat                                     | Mitigation                                                                                                                      | Status   |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| Values leave the device without the person | On-device OCR, coding, analysis and export; the only network calls are the two optional ones above, each behind its own consent | met      |
| Backups or iCloud carry the store          | Store excluded from backup; `NSFileProtectionComplete` default; exports and diagnostics written with complete protection        | met      |
| The app switcher shows values              | `PrivacyCover.swift` covers the window when the app is not active                                                               | met      |
| Logs carry values                          | Log lines carry counts and codes only (`Logging.swift`)                                                                         | met      |
| A cloud question identifies the person     | At most 40 values, no name, date of birth or insurance number; the service enforces the same (`CloudAnalysis.swift`, ADR-034)   | met      |
| Transfer to a third country                | Default on device; hosted default Azure OpenAI in the EU data zone; the Anthropic option is opt-in and says "United States"     | partly   |
| Screenshots or screen recording            | Not prevented (iOS allows no reliable block)                                                                                    | accepted |

### Denial of service

| Threat                           | Mitigation                                                                                                                             | Status   |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| The hub is down                  | The app works without the hub; the record is on the device                                                                             | met      |
| A hostile scan floods the parser | Vision and the parser run on bounded images; a degraded scan loses rows, never hangs (`ScanningTests.swift`, `AccuracyBenchmarkTests`) | met      |
| Lost phone                       | Export in four formats for the person to keep; no recovery from the hub by design                                                      | accepted |

### Elevation of privilege

| Threat                                  | Mitigation                                                                                             | Status |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------ |
| Debug entry points in a release build   | `-MBSelfTest`, `-MBDemoSeed`, `-MBShot` are compiled out (`#if DEBUG`)                                 | met    |
| The app writes to Apple Health          | Read-only authorisation (`WearableSource.swift`); pinned by `SecurityPostureTests`                     | met    |
| The app token does more than the record | The hub scopes the token to the sandbox record of that account; `isSandboxUsername` on every app route | met    |

## Residual risks and what closes them

1. **App lock**: decided and implemented 2026-10-15 (ADR-060). (TR-03161 O.Auth)
2. **No tamper or jailbreak detection**: declined with reasons in ADR-060; the sealed store and App Attest are the controls. (O.Resi)
3. **No certificate pinning**: declined with reasons in ADR-060; ATS without an exception domain, managed rotation. (O.Ntwk)
4. **Hosted Anthropic option.** Opt-in, named on screen, but a transfer to the
   United States; the operator needs a transfer basis or must switch it off.
5. **Independent test.** This model and the tests are the project's own. An
   independent penetration test against a release build on a device, and the
   requirement-level TR-03161 gap list, remain open; see
   [`security-test-report-2026-10-15.md`](/docs/security/security-test-report).

# Klarbefund: self-assessment

Data protection, security and regulatory status of the Klarbefund iPhone app,
assessed by the project itself against the code in `clients/ios/` as of
2026-10-15. **This is a self-assessment, not a certification, an audit or a
legal opinion.** Every "met" below points to the code or test that shows it;
anything not shown is marked open. Accuracy evidence is in
[`evidence.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence); running it on a Mac in [`run-on-mac.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-run-on-mac).
The code references below were last checked against the sources on 2026-10-15,
the same day the evidence was last produced (see the run record in
[`evidence.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence#run-record)).

Status values: **met** (implemented and shown in code or tests), **partly**
(implemented in part, or shown only by design), **open** (not done), **n/a**
(does not apply to this app).

## Scope

| In scope                                                                        | Out of scope                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| The iOS app (`clients/ios/Sources/MeinBefund`, `Sources/Shared`), release build | The demo hub and its Azure deployment, assessed separately (ADR-045, BSI C5 notes in the CI workflows) |
| Its optional calls to the hub (EHDS connect, ADR-049/054)                       | Apple's platform (iOS, Secure Enclave, HealthKit), relied on as provided                               |
| Its optional call to the cloud explanation service (ADR-034)                    | The model providers behind that service                                                                |

## Data protection (GDPR)

The data processed is health data, a special category under Art. 9 GDPR.

| Principle                                                | Status | How the app meets it                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Where                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Data protection by default (Art. 25)                     | met    | No account. Scanning, OCR, coding, storage and export run on the device; nothing leaves it unless the person sends it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `Scanning.swift`, `ReportStore.swift`, `OnDeviceAnalysis.swift`                   |
| Data minimisation (Art. 5(1)(c))                         | met    | The store holds no name, birth date or insurance number. A cloud question carries only the values the person ticks, at most 40, and no identifying field; the service enforces this again server-side.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | `Sources/Shared/CloudAnalysis.swift`, `CloudAnalysisContractTests.swift`, ADR-034 |
| Purpose limitation and consent (Art. 6, 9(2)(a))         | met    | Study participation, ePA objection and registry/research use are separate consents, each revocable. A cloud call names its provider in the request itself, so a blanket setting cannot stand in for it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `Sources/Shared/Consents.swift`, `ConsentsTests.swift`, `CloudConsentSheet.swift` |
| Rights of access, portability, erasure (Art. 15, 17, 20) | met    | Full export (JSON, FHIR R4, OMOP CDM, PDF) and full deletion from the app; an EHDS hub account the app created can be deleted by it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | `DataExport.swift`, `ReportExport.swift`, `OmopExportTests.swift`, ADR-054        |
| Security of processing (Art. 32)                         | met    | See the security section.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                   |
| Transparency (Art. 13)                                   | partly | Permission texts in English and German, privacy manifest declares health data, not linked, not tracked. A full privacy notice for an operator is not part of the repository.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | `project.yml` (usage strings), `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`, `LegalViews.swift`        |
| Transfer to third countries (Art. 44 ff.)                | partly | Default is on device: nothing is transferred. The person can switch at any time to the hosted service, whose default is Azure OpenAI in the EU data zone (`DataZoneStandard`, no transfer), or to their own Azure OpenAI resource or their own Anthropic key. Only Anthropic, hosted or own key, processes in the United States; the app says so on the settings screen. For the hosted Anthropic option the operator needs a processor agreement and a transfer basis. | `ProviderSettings.swift`, `services/claude-federation/src/providers.ts`, ADR-034  |
| Records of processing, DPIA (Art. 30, 35)                | open   | No record of processing and no DPIA. A DPIA is likely required for any operator (health data, new technology). The project can supply a template; the operator owns it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |                                                                                   |
| Controller role                                          | open   | Using the app on one's own device is personal use. Whoever runs the cloud explanation service or a hub the app connects to is a controller or processor and must be named.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |                                                                                   |

## Security: BSI TR-03161 part 1 (mobile applications)

Assessed at the level of the test objective groups of
[TR-03161 part 1, version 3.0](https://www.bsi.bund.de/EN/Themen/Unternehmen-und-Organisationen/Standards-und-Zertifizierung/Technische-Richtlinien/TR-nach-Thema-sortiert/tr03161/tr-03161.html).
A certification maps each individual requirement against the official PDF and
is carried out by a BSI-recognised test laboratory; this table is the input to
that gap analysis, not a replacement for it.

| Group                         | Status | Evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Gap                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| O.Purp: purpose, minimisation | met    | Purpose stated in the app and `README.md` ("Not a medical device"); minimisation and per-call consent as above; no tracking (`NSPrivacyTracking` false).                                                                                                                                                            | Formal intended-purpose statement (see regulation).                                                                                  |
| O.Arch: architecture          | met    | On-device by default; the phone holds no API credential (ADR-034); hub accounts only from an App Attest-verified app (ADR-054); provenance model keeps OCR values `preliminary` (`Provenance.swift`).                                                                                                               | Threat model written: `docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund.md`.                                                                    |
| O.Source: source code         | partly | CodeQL on every iOS change (`codeql-swift.yml`, `Scripts/codeql-swift.sh`; 0 findings on 2026-10-15); debug-only launch arguments compiled out of release builds (`#if DEBUG`); Swift 6 strict concurrency; `SecurityPostureTests` pin the build settings this table cites.                                         | No obfuscation (open source by design; argue as not applicable).                                                                     |
| O.TrdP: third-party software  | met    | No third-party package at all: `Package.swift` and `project.yml` declare no external dependency; only Apple frameworks.                                                                                                                                                                                             | SBOM: `docs/sbom/klarbefund-ios.cdx.json`, regenerated by `scripts/security/generate-sbom.sh --check`.                               |
| O.Cryp: cryptography          | met    | Only Apple CryptoKit: each record sealed with AES-GCM under a 256-bit key; key in the Keychain as `WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly`; no own cryptography (`ReportStore.swift`, export-compliance note in `project.yml`).                                                                                                 |                                                                                                                                      |
| O.Rand: random numbers        | met    | Keys from `SymmetricKey(size: .bits256)`, Apple's system RNG.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |                                                                                                                                      |
| O.Auth: authentication        | met    | No local account. Hub: OIDC with PKCE in `ASWebAuthenticationSession` (`OIDCSession.swift`), device grant with Keycloak consent (ADR-049), App Attest (ADR-054); tokens in the Keychain, `ThisDeviceOnly` (`EHDSConnection.swift`).                                                                                 | App lock since 2026-10-15: Face ID or Touch ID, passcode as fallback, on by default (`AppLock.swift`, `AppLockPolicy`, ADR-060).     |
| O.Pass: passwords             | n/a    | The app handles no passwords; sign-in happens in the system web session.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |                                                                                                                                      |
| O.Data: data at rest          | met    | `NSFileProtectionComplete` as the default data protection (entitlement); records AES-GCM sealed; store excluded from backup; exports and diagnostics written with complete protection; app switcher covered (`PrivacyCover.swift`); log lines carry counts and codes only. A cable test failed to copy stored data. | Independent verification of the cable test.                                                                                          |
| O.Paid: paid resources        | n/a    | No in-app purchases.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |                                                                                                                                      |
| O.Ntwk: network               | partly | App Transport Security on, exception only for local networking (`project.yml`); all hub and service calls over HTTPS.                                                                                                                                                                                               | No certificate pinning, declined with reasons in ADR-060 (ATS, no exception domain, managed rotation).                               |
| O.Resi: resilience            | open   | App Attest proves app integrity to the hub, not to the app itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | No jailbreak or debugger detection, declined with reasons in ADR-060 (bypassable; the sealed store and App Attest are the controls). |
| O.Plat: platform              | met    | Camera and HealthKit asked for at the moment of use, HealthKit read-only with no copy kept; no notifications; app switcher covered.                                                                                                                                                                                 |                                                                                                                                      |

Backend parts (TR-03161 part 3) apply to the cloud explanation service and the
hub, not to the app, and are out of scope here. TR-03161 certification is
mandatory for a DiGA; Klarbefund is not one (see below).

## Regulation

| Framework                                     | Assessment                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Status                                                     |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Medical device (MDR 2017/745 / IVDR 2017/746) | Intended purpose as stated: store, display and export the values a laboratory printed, and explain what a measurement is. No diagnosis, risk assessment, prognosis or treatment advice; no normal/abnormal verdict. Under MDCG 2019-11 Rev.1 storage, communication and display of data is generally not a medical device function. Because the values come from in-vitro samples, the IVDR, not MDR rule 11, would apply if it qualified (ADR-034). **Borderline:** the trends screen colours values against published bands (ADR-039). The project's position is that a comparison with a quoted, sourced number is not a finding. | partly: written qualification and an external opinion open |
| DiGA (§ 139e SGB V)                           | Not applicable: a DiGA must be a CE-marked medical device, and Klarbefund is deliberately not one. Consequently no DiGA-specific certificates (ISO 27001, ISO 13485, TR-03161) are claimed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | n/a                                                        |
| EU AI Act (2024/1689)                         | The optional explanation feature uses a language model, on device by default or a named cloud provider. As long as the app is not a medical device it is not a high-risk system under Art. 6(1). Transparency: the answer must be recognisable as AI-generated (Art. 50). A hosted answer ends with "Answered by <provider>, model <model>" (`CloudConsentSheet.swift`); the on-device answer says "Answered by on-device, model Apple on-device model" through the same footer (`OnDeviceAnalysis.swift`); `SecurityPostureTests` pins both.                                                                                        | met: every answer names provider and model                 |
| EHDS (2025/327)                               | Primary use: the app reads the person's own record from the hub with consent (ADR-049). If the app is ever offered as claiming interoperability with EHR systems, it becomes a wellness application under [Art. 47](https://www.ringholm.com/ehds/article-47.htm) and needs the label described there.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | n/a today                                                  |
| Apple distribution                            | TestFlight build approved by Apple's beta review for external testers (ADR-050); privacy manifest and App Privacy label declare health data, not linked, not tracked.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | met                                                        |

## What would close the open items

Done on 2026-10-15, by the project itself (see
[`docs/security/security-test-report-2026-10-15.md`](/docs/security/security-test-report)):
the threat model, the SBOM, a configuration test suite, and a self-conducted
security test with CodeQL, Semgrep, grype, trivy, gitleaks and anonymous
black-box checks of the hub. Still open:

1. Written intended-purpose statement and MDCG 2019-11 qualification, with an
   external opinion on the trends colouring.
2. Hosted explanation service: name the operator as controller or processor,
   sign the processor agreement with Azure (EU data zone, the default), and for
   the opt-in Anthropic option document the transfer basis or switch it off.
3. DPIA template and data-flow diagram for an operator.
4. An **independent** penetration test (a release build on a device, the
   hub as each role in office hours), and the requirement-level TR-03161
   part 1 gap list against the official PDF. The self-conducted test says
   what such a test would add.
5. Done 2026-10-15 (ADR-060): the app lock is implemented, on by default;
   certificate pinning and jailbreak detection are declined with written
   reasons. Remaining for a laboratory: judge those reasons.

# Klarbefund: evidence

What a reviewer outside this project can check about Klarbefund, the iPhone
lab-report scanner ([#186](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/issues/186)),
and what is still missing. Written for an insurer's, a hospital's or an
auditor's first question: _is the extraction right, is the data safe, and is
this a medical device?_ Data protection, BSI TR-03161 and regulation are
assessed in [`self-assessment.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment); how to run all of this
on a Mac is in [`run-on-mac.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-run-on-mac). The person-facing description is in
[`README.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/klarbefund/README.md), the developer side in
[`clients/ios/README.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/README.md).

Klarbefund is open source under the [Apache License 2.0](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/LICENSE). The
project is not a vendor: there is no company behind it, no support contract and
no warranty. Whoever deploys the app, or a fork of it, operates it and carries
the data protection and security duties that come with that.

## Status

- At the HL7 AI Challenge 2026 submission (deadline 2026-06-30) Klarbefund
  was a prototype. The award ("Open Solution") went to the EHDS platform in
  this repository.
- In the winner presentation the app was shown as a live demo.
- It is in TestFlight, approved by Apple's beta review for external testers
  ([ADR-050](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-050-klarbefund-beta-by-public-testflight-link.md)).
- It reads Apple Health (HealthKit, read only) and connects to the demo hub,
  whose secondary use runs in the hub's Secure Processing Environment
  ([ADR-054](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-054-klarbefund-creates-a-sandbox-account-with-app-attest.md)).

## What is already evidenced

| Claim                                                        | Evidence                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A degraded scan loses rows, it never invents values          | `Tests/SharedTests/ScanningTests.swift`: synthetic sheets under skew, glare, dim light, blur and low resolution, read with Vision; any coded value not on the sheet fails |
| German number rules (decimal comma, `1.240` = 1240, `0.300`) | `Tests/SharedTests/LabLineParserTests.swift`                                                                                                                              |
| The unit selects the LOINC code; urine is never serum        | `LabLineParserTests.swift`, `RealScanLessonsTests.swift` (layouts of 19 real scans, every value invented)                                                                 |
| Nothing is dropped silently                                  | Self-test (`-MBSelfTest`, 27 checks): every printed row ends up coded, unmapped or unread                                                                                 |
| OCR values stay preliminary                                  | Provenance model (`Sources/Shared/Provenance.swift`): only a laboratory's own PDF text layer yields FHIR `final`                                                          |
| A real scan can be replayed without the phone or the image   | `swift run ScanReplay`, `swift run LabFile`; both refuse paths inside this repository                                                                                     |
| Exports are standard                                         | FHIR R4 bundle with LOINC and UCUM (`FhirBundleParityTests.swift`), OMOP CDM v5.4 (`OmopExportTests.swift`)                                                               |
| Data stays on the device by default                          | On-device OCR and analysis, per-item encryption, no iCloud backup, separate consents, export and deletion ([README](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/klarbefund/README.md#privacy-and-safety))                        |

## Measuring accuracy

`ExtractionAccuracy` (`clients/ios/Sources/Shared/ExtractionAccuracy.swift`)
compares an extraction with a hand-checked truth, field by field: value with
its comparator, unit, LOINC code (or the expected refusal), printed reference
range and laboratory date. Its headline numbers:

- **exact**: rows right in every checked field;
- **silent errors**: rows that were coded, so shown as a value, and wrong in
  value, unit or code. This is the number that matters clinically; the target
  is zero;
- **spurious**: coded values with no row on the sheet behind them;
- **missed** and **unread**: rows lost, and lines handed to the reviewer.

Two ways to run it:

1. **Synthetic benchmark, in CI.** `AccuracyBenchmarkTests` renders the
   synthetic panel under nine scan conditions, reads it with Vision and asserts
   zero silent errors under each. Locally: `cd clients/ios && swift test`; with
   `KLARBEFUND_BENCHMARK_OUT=<file>` set, the counts are written there as JSON.
   An `ios-unit-tests` job for `.github/workflows/test.yml` (pending, YAML in
   [`run-on-mac.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-run-on-mac#4-put-the-swift-suite-into-ci)) runs the
   whole Swift suite on `macos-26` and keeps that JSON as the
   `klarbefund-accuracy-benchmark` artifact; until it lands, CI builds only the
   `Shared` target. No real data is involved, so the JSON can be published as
   it is.
2. **Pilot on real reports, never in the repository.** A participant exports
   diagnostics from the app (ADR-038), and a `truth.json` is written beside each
   `diagnostics.json` from the paper:

   ```json
   {
     "schema": 1,
     "labDate": "2026-09-12",
     "rows": [
       {
         "label": "LDL-Cholesterin",
         "value": 141,
         "unit": "mg/dl",
         "loinc": "2089-1",
         "referenceText": "< 116"
       },
       {
         "label": "Ferritin",
         "value": 10,
         "comparator": "<",
         "unit": "ug/l",
         "loinc": "2276-4"
       },
       {
         "label": "Natrium [U]",
         "value": 80,
         "unit": "mmol/l",
         "loinc": null,
         "refused": true
       }
     ]
   }
   ```

   ```bash
   cd clients/ios
   swift run ScanReplay ~/Pilot/export --truth          # per row: which fields were wrong, no values
   swift run ScanReplay ~/Pilot/export --truth --json   # counts only, the part to publish
   ```

   Only the counts leave the participant's folder. Before a report is used:
   written consent from the participant (purpose, retention, withdrawal, and
   whether values go to an explanation service), and a check that the study the
   report comes from does not restrict sharing its results.

Target values per field are fixed before a pilot is measured, and the pilot's
sample size is stated next to every number.

## Run record

The checklist in [`run-on-mac.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-run-on-mac) was last run on 2026-10-15 at
commit `1474295d` of this branch, on macOS 26.7.1 with Xcode 26 (Swift 6.4).
Everything below is the synthetic benchmark; no real report was involved, so the
counts are published as they are in
[`accuracy-benchmark.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/klarbefund/accuracy-benchmark.json), the file the run wrote.
This is the project checking itself: a reviewer reproduces it with the same
three commands, and a pilot on real reports is still open.

| Step                      | Result                                                |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `swift build`             | Shared, AnalyteParity, ScanReplay and LabFile built   |
| `swift run AnalyteParity` | parity ok: 1589 codings, 71 units                     |
| `swift test`              | 319 tests in 54 suites passed, 0 failures, about 10 s |

One synthetic panel of 8 rows, read with Vision under nine conditions, 72
truth rows in all. `AccuracyBenchmarkTests` asserts zero silent errors under
each condition; the other columns are reported, not asserted.

| Condition          | Found | Exact | Silent errors | Spurious | Unread lines | Reference right |
| ------------------ | ----: | ----: | ------------: | -------: | -----------: | --------------: |
| clean 150 dpi scan |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |            0 |           8 / 8 |
| skewed 1 degree    |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |            0 |           8 / 8 |
| skewed 2 degrees   |     7 |     5 |             0 |        0 |            0 |           5 / 7 |
| skewed 5 degrees   |     5 |     0 |             0 |        0 |            2 |           0 / 5 |
| dim room           |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |            0 |           8 / 8 |
| flash glare        |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |            0 |           8 / 8 |
| slight motion blur |     7 |     7 |             0 |        0 |            1 |           7 / 7 |
| heavy blur         |     0 |     0 |             0 |        0 |            0 |           0 / 0 |
| low resolution     |     7 |     6 |             0 |        0 |            1 |           7 / 7 |
| **all nine**       |    58 |    50 |         **0** |    **0** |            4 |         51 / 58 |

What the numbers say: a clean, dim, glaring or slightly skewed sheet is read
in full and exactly. As the sheet degrades the app loses rows, first in the
reference-range column, then whole rows, until heavy blur yields nothing at
all. At no point does it show a value, unit or code that is wrong, which is
the property the suite enforces.

One finding from the run itself: the test target did not compile with
Swift 6.4, because `Comparator` had become ambiguous between `Shared` and the
platform SDK. The test now names `Shared.Comparator`, as `OmopExportTests`
already did.

## Open

| Topic                                      | What is missing                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Intended purpose (MDR)                     | A written qualification under MDCG 2019-11 Rev.1. The borderline is the trends screen, which colours values against published bands (ADR-039); the project's position is that a comparison with a quoted number is not a finding. An external opinion.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Operator of the hosted explanation service | Explanations run on the device by default. The person can switch to the hosted service (default Azure OpenAI, EU data zone; Anthropic opt-in, United States) or to their own Azure OpenAI or Anthropic account. Whoever runs the hosted service processes health data and must document that role (records of processing, processor agreements).                                                                                |
| Data protection                            | Data-flow diagram and a data protection impact assessment template for an operator.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| Security                                   | Threat model, SBOM and a self-conducted security test exist since 2026-10-15 (`docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund.md`, `docs/sbom/`, `docs/security/security-test-report-2026-10-15.md`). The app locks with Face ID or the passcode since 2026-10-15 (ADR-060). Open: an independent penetration test and the requirement-level gap list against BSI TR-03161 part 1. CodeQL runs on every iOS change (`codeql-swift.yml`). |
| Pilot accuracy                             | Truth files and aggregate counts from real reports, as above.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

# Klarbefund: evidence report for health insurers

Date 2026-10-15. Prepared by the project for a statutory or private health
insurer, a hospital group or an ePA vendor who asks the same three
questions: _is the extraction right, is the data safe, and is this a
medical device?_ Everything here is produced by tools that anyone can run on
the repository, with the commands given, and every open item is named as
open. The one-page version for a steering meeting is the summary table; the
rest is the evidence behind each line.

**What is on offer.** Klarbefund is a demo environment and an open-source
reference implementation (Apache 2.0). It is not a product with a vendor
behind it. What the project offers an insurer is either a **white-label
version** of the app, under the insurer's name and operator responsibility,
or **technical consulting** to integrate the scanner, the coding dictionary
and the FHIR writer into an ePA or EHR app the insurer already runs. Both
paths start from the evidence below.

## Summary

| Question                                  | Answer, with the evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Status                                  |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Does it read laboratory values correctly? | Synthetic benchmark under nine scan conditions: 0 silent errors, 0 invented values, 50 of 72 rows exact; degraded scans lose rows, they never show a wrong value. 1751 analyte codings, 71 units, LOINC and UCUM.                                                      | evidenced, pilot on real reports open   |
| Is the data safe?                         | On the device by default, Face ID or passcode in front of the results, AES-GCM per record, key in the Secure Enclave-backed Keychain, no third-party package, read-only Apple Health. CodeQL 0 findings, 0 known vulnerabilities, 9 posture tests, threat model, SBOM. | self-tested, independent test open      |
| Is it a medical device?                   | Intended purpose: store, display, export and explain what a measurement is; no diagnosis, no verdict. Under MDCG 2019-11 generally not a device; the trends colouring is the borderline the project has written down.                                                  | position written, external opinion open |
| Does it fit the ePA and the EHDS?         | FHIR R4 with LOINC, UCUM, SNOMED CT, CVX and ATC; the test database now carries four of the five EHDS Art. 14 priority categories; the hub exports the whole record in one Bundle; Art. 47 wellness label applies if marketed as interoperable.                        | yes                                     |
| Is it a DiGA?                             | No, by design: a DiGA must be a CE-marked device. No DiGA certificates are claimed.                                                                                                                                                                                    | n/a                                     |
| Can my team verify this?                  | Yes: every number has a command, the scans and tests run on a Mac with Xcode, and the hub's API collection (Bruno) rehearses the integration.                                                                                                                          | yes                                     |

## 1. What Klarbefund does

A person photographs a laboratory report or opens the laboratory's PDF.
The app reads it on the device, codes every row with LOINC and UCUM, keeps
the printed reference range, shows trends across reports, and exports the
record as FHIR R4, OMOP CDM, JSON or PDF. Values read from a photograph stay
`preliminary` until the person checks them; only a laboratory's own PDF
text layer yields `final`. With consent the app writes the person's record
into their own account on the EHDS demo hub, and weekly means from Apple
Health beside it. Nothing leaves the phone otherwise.

Details: [`README.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/klarbefund/README.md) (person-facing),
[`clients/ios/README.md`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/clients/ios/README.md) (developer),
[`evidence.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence), [`self-assessment.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment).

## 2. Accuracy

The measure is `ExtractionAccuracy`: a field-by-field comparison with a
hand-checked truth, value, unit, code, reference range and date. The number
that matters clinically is **silent errors**, rows the app showed as a value
and got wrong; the benchmark asserts zero under every condition.

| Condition          | Found | Exact | Silent errors | Spurious |
| ------------------ | ----: | ----: | ------------: | -------: |
| clean 150 dpi scan |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |
| skewed 1 degree    |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |
| skewed 2 degrees   |     7 |     5 |             0 |        0 |
| skewed 5 degrees   |     5 |     0 |             0 |        0 |
| dim room           |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |
| flash glare        |     8 |     8 |             0 |        0 |
| slight motion blur |     7 |     7 |             0 |        0 |
| heavy blur         |     0 |     0 |             0 |        0 |
| low resolution     |     7 |     6 |             0 |        0 |
| **all nine**       |    58 |    50 |         **0** |    **0** |

Synthetic sheets, 8 rows each, read with Apple Vision, 2026-10-15
([`accuracy-benchmark.json`](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/klarbefund/accuracy-benchmark.json)). A pilot on real
reports, with written consent and only counts leaving the participant's
folder, is designed ([`evidence.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence#measuring-accuracy)) and
not yet run; an insurer's own pilot is the natural next step.

## 3. Security and data protection

| Layer                 | What was done                                                                                                                                                   | Result, 2026-10-15                                          |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Static analysis       | CodeQL over the app (82 Swift files); CodeQL and Semgrep over the hub in CI                                                                                     | 0 findings                                                  |
| Dependencies          | CycloneDX bills for the app and every hub service ([`docs/sbom/`](/docs/security/sbom)); grype and npm audit against them                                         | 0 known vulnerabilities; the app has 0 third-party packages |
| Secrets               | gitleaks over the tree and the last 200 commits                                                                                                                 | 0 after review                                              |
| Containers, manifests | trivy over Dockerfiles and Kubernetes manifests                                                                                                                 | 0 HIGH after two fixes; 2 MEDIUM, 12 LOW accepted or open   |
| Build configuration   | `SecurityPostureTests`: entitlements, privacy manifest, ATS, cryptography, PKCE, HealthKit read-only, export compliance                                         | 11 of 11 pass                                               |
| Threat model          | STRIDE for the app ([`threat-model-klarbefund.md`](/docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund)) beside the hub's                                                    | written; residual risks listed                              |
| Live hub, outside     | 40 anonymous black-box checks: route gates, redirects, headers, TLS, Keycloak console                                                                           | TLS and console checks pass; gate checks need office hours  |
| GDPR                  | Art. 25 by default, Art. 5 minimisation, Art. 6/9 consents, Art. 15/17/20 rights: met in code; transparency and transfers partly; DPIA and controller role open | see [`self-assessment.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment)              |
| BSI TR-03161 part 1   | Assessed by objective group: 9 met, 3 partly, 1 open (resilience, declined with reasons in ADR-060), 2 n/a                                                      | input to a laboratory's gap analysis                        |

The full method, findings and fixes are in
[`security-test-report-2026-10-15.md`](/docs/security/security-test-report).
It is the project testing itself. An independent penetration test, which
an insurer will rightly ask for, is listed there with what it would add.

## 4. Regulatory position

| Framework           | Position                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Open                                    |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| MDR / IVDR          | Storage, display, export and explanation of what a measurement is; no diagnosis, risk score or treatment advice. Generally not a device under MDCG 2019-11 Rev.1. The trends screen colours values against published, sourced bands; the project's position is that a comparison with a quoted number is not a finding. | written qualification, external opinion |
| DiGA (§ 139e SGB V) | Not applicable; deliberately not a device                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | none                                    |
| EU AI Act           | Not high-risk while not a device; every answer, on device or hosted, names its provider and model (Art. 50)                                                                                                                                                                                                             | none                                    |
| EHDS 2025/327       | Art. 3 record access with consent; Art. 47 wellness label if marketed as interoperable with EHR systems                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | label text when marketed                |
| Apple               | TestFlight beta approved for external testers; App Privacy label: health data, not linked, not tracked                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | none                                    |

## 5. The test database, and the kinds of result it holds

The demo hub runs on 127 synthetic patients (Synthea) plus hand-seeded
records, in a Neo4j graph that mirrors FHIR R4 and OMOP CDM. On 2026-10-15
it gained the four result types an ePA integrator asks for first (ADR-059).

| Result type                               | Coding             | In the app     | In the test database | How an integrator gets it                         |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------ | -------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Laboratory, blood and urine               | LOINC, UCUM        | yes            | yes                  | `/api/patient/observations`, FHIR Bundle          |
| Resting ECG, Holter                       | LOINC 11524-6, EC  | yes            | **new**              | `include=all`, DiagnosticReport with Observations |
| Spirometry, CPET, stress test, lactate    | LOINC, PF and EC   | yes            | planned              |                                                   |
| DXA body composition                      | LOINC 38269-7, RAD | yes            | planned              |                                                   |
| Continuous glucose monitoring             | LOINC 107930-0     | yes            | planned              |                                                   |
| 24 h blood pressure, device screens       | LOINC              | yes            | planned              |                                                   |
| Wearable weekly means                     | LOINC              | yes            | yes                  | written by the app (ADR-057)                      |
| Imaging reports (X-ray, echo, ultrasound) | LOINC, RAD         | no (narrative) | **new**              | `include=all`, DiagnosticReport with conclusion   |
| Vaccination record                        | CVX                | no             | **new**              | `include=all`, Immunization                       |
| Medication plan (BMP)                     | ATC, 1-0-1 dosing  | no             | **new**              | `include=all`, MedicationStatement                |
| Conditions, medications                   | SNOMED CT, RxNorm  | via hub        | yes                  | profile API, `$everything`                        |

Candidates after these, by EHDS Art. 14 category: microbiology, allergy
panels, genetics (laboratory results); pathology, sleep studies, ECG
narratives (reports); patient-reported outcomes and discharge letters
(patient summary, discharge reports). Each is one seed file and one mapper.

Rehearsal: `bruno/MVHDv2/01 Patient/06 My whole record` pulls the Bundle
with all four categories and fails loudly when a category is missing.

## 6. Integration paths

1. **White-label app.** The app as it is, renamed and signed by the insurer,
   with the insurer as operator: privacy notice, DPIA, processor agreement
   for the hosted explanation service (Azure OpenAI, EU data zone, by
   default), and the Apple account. The code stays open source.
2. **Components into an existing ePA or EHR app.** The `Shared` Swift
   package (scanning, the 1751-coding dictionary, provenance, FHIR and OMOP
   writers, consents) has no third-party dependency and is covered by 419
   tests; it drops into an existing iOS app. The same dictionary exists in
   TypeScript (`services/epa-ingest`) for a server-side path.
3. **Hub-side only.** An insurer's platform reads the record as FHIR R4
   from the hub's API, or runs the ePA ingest CLI against PDFs it already
   holds, without the app.

In every path the insurer owns the data protection roles; the project
supplies the templates and the evidence.

## 7. What is still open

| Item                                            | Who closes it                      |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Independent penetration test, TR-03161 gap list | a BSI-recognised laboratory        |
| Pilot accuracy on real reports                  | the insurer's pilot, with consents |
| Written MDR qualification, external opinion     | regulatory counsel                 |
| DPIA, records of processing, controller role    | the operator                       |
| Profile page sections for the new result types  | the project                        |
| Swift suite in CI (needs workflow rights)       | the repository owner               |

## 8. Verify it yourself

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2 && cd MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2
cd clients/ios && swift test                                   # 419 tests, incl. the benchmark and the posture tests
cd ../.. && scripts/security/scan-repo.sh                      # SBOM check, grype, trivy, gitleaks, semgrep, hadolint, npm audit
scripts/security/check-hub-blackbox.sh                         # the live hub from outside, office hours Mon-Fri 05:17-18:13 UTC
./scripts/run-api-tests.sh Local "01 Patient"                  # the record as an integrator receives it
```

Documents: [`evidence.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence), [`self-assessment.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment),
[`run-on-mac.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-run-on-mac), [`security-test-report-2026-10-15.md`](/docs/security/security-test-report),
[`threat-model-klarbefund.md`](/docs/security/threat-model-klarbefund),
[ADR-059](https://github.com/ma3u/MinimumViableHealthDataspacev2/blob/main/docs/ADRs/ADR-059-the-record-holds-reports-vaccinations-and-the-medication-plan.md).

docs.title: Klarbefund: running the evidence on a Mac
docs.summary: How to reproduce every number in the evidence on a Mac with Xcode.
docs.markdown:
# Klarbefund: running the evidence on a Mac

The Swift package targets macOS 26 and iOS 26, and the scanning and benchmark
tests need Apple's Vision framework, so they run only on a Mac. This is the
checklist for producing the evidence in [`evidence.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence) and
[`self-assessment.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment) on one.

## Prerequisites

| What                | Why                                                 | Check                                |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| macOS 26            | `Package.swift` declares `.macOS("26.0")`           | `sw_vers -productVersion`            |
| Xcode 26, selected  | Swift 6 toolchain and the macOS 26 SDK with Vision  | `xcode-select -p`, `swift --version` |
| XcodeGen (app only) | generates `MeinBefund.xcodeproj` from `project.yml` | `brew install xcodegen`              |
| CodeQL (optional)   | the static analysis the pre-push hook and CI run    | `brew install --cask codeql`         |

Nothing else: the package has no third-party dependencies, so there is nothing
to resolve or download.

## 1. Build and test

```bash
git fetch origin && git switch feat/186-klarbefund-accuracy-evidence
cd clients/ios

swift build                       # Shared, ScanReplay, LabFile, AnalyteParity
swift run AnalyteParity           # the Swift dictionary matches its TypeScript source
KLARBEFUND_BENCHMARK_OUT=$HOME/Desktop/klarbefund-accuracy-benchmark.json swift test
```

`swift test` runs the whole suite, 319 tests in 54 suites. The scanning and
benchmark suites render A4 sheets and read them with Vision, serially; on an
Apple-silicon Mac the whole suite took about ten seconds after the build. Two suites are new on this branch:

- `ExtractionAccuracyTests`: the accuracy measure itself, no Vision needed;
- `AccuracyBenchmarkTests`: nine scan conditions, zero silent errors required
  under each, counts written to the JSON file named above.

Only that JSON is evidence to publish: synthetic sheets, counts and LOINC codes,
no values. To run one suite: `swift test --filter AccuracyBenchmarkTests`.

## 2. Pilot on real reports (outside the repository)

1. In the app: menu → **Export diagnostics**, AirDrop the zip to the Mac.
2. Unzip it **outside the repository**, for example `~/Pilot/klarbefund-diagnostics-…`.
3. Next to each `diagnostics.json`, write a `truth.json` from the paper (format
   in [`evidence.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-evidence#measuring-accuracy)).
4. Run:

   ```bash
   swift run ScanReplay ~/Pilot/klarbefund-diagnostics-2026-10-20 --truth          # per row, no values
   swift run ScanReplay ~/Pilot/klarbefund-diagnostics-2026-10-20 --truth --json   # counts only
   ```

Both tools refuse a path inside `clients/ios/`. Get each participant's written
consent before step 1, and delete the export when the counts are taken.

## 3. Optional checks

```bash
Scripts/codeql-swift.sh           # CodeQL on the app, ~15 minutes, exits 1 on a new finding
Scripts/run-ui-tests.sh           # XCUITest on a simulator, demo data only
xcrun simctl launch <udid> red.mabu.meinbefund -MBSelfTest   # 27-check self-test, see clients/ios/README.md
```

## 4. Put the Swift suite into CI

CI today builds only the `Shared` target (`ios-analyte-parity` in
`.github/workflows/test.yml`); it never runs `swift test`. Add this job after
`ios-analyte-parity` and push it with an account allowed to change workflows:

```yaml
ios-unit-tests:
  name: iOS Unit Tests + Accuracy Benchmark (Swift)
  runs-on: macos-26
  defaults:
    run:
      working-directory: ./clients/ios
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7
    - name: Swift version
      run: swift --version
    - name: Run unit tests
      env:
        KLARBEFUND_BENCHMARK_OUT: ${{ runner.temp }}/klarbefund-accuracy-benchmark.json
      run: swift test
    - name: Upload accuracy benchmark
      if: always()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
      with:
        name: klarbefund-accuracy-benchmark
        path: ${{ runner.temp }}/klarbefund-accuracy-benchmark.json
        if-no-files-found: warn
```

The benchmark JSON then becomes a downloadable artifact of every run that
touches `clients/ios/`, which is the reproducible form an outside reviewer can
check.

## 5. What to bring back

- the `swift test` summary line, and any failure in full;
- `klarbefund-accuracy-benchmark.json`;
- for the pilot, the `--truth --json` output and the number of participants and
  sheets.

# BSI C5 Gap Analysis — EHDS Integration Hub

**Standard**: BSI Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue (C5:2020)
**Relevance**: EHDS Art. 50(6) requires HDAB-approved dataspaces to meet C5 or equivalent.
**Scope**: Demo/MVP assessment. Full production audit requires accredited C5 auditor.

---

## Status Legend

| Symbol | Meaning                           |
| ------ | --------------------------------- |
| ✅     | Implemented (demo)                |
| 🟡     | Partially implemented             |
| ⚠️     | Accepted risk for demo            |
| ❌     | Not applicable or not implemented |
| 🔵     | Production roadmap only           |

---

## C5 Control Domains

### OIS — Organisational and Information Security

| Control | Requirement          | Demo Status | Gap / Mitigation                              |
| ------- | -------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| OIS-01  | IS policy documented | ✅          | This document + threat model                  |
| OIS-02  | IS roles assigned    | ⚠️          | Fictional personas only; no real CISO         |
| OIS-03  | Risk assessment      | ✅          | threat-model.md + STRIDE analysis             |
| OIS-04  | Asset inventory      | ✅          | Assets listed in threat model                 |
| OIS-05  | Supplier security    | ⚠️          | Neo4j, Keycloak, NATS — not formally assessed |

### CCM — Change Management

| Control | Requirement                | Demo Status | Gap / Mitigation                  |
| ------- | -------------------------- | ----------- | --------------------------------- |
| CCM-01  | Change process documented  | ✅          | Git workflow + PR reviews         |
| CCM-02  | Security review on changes | 🟡          | This phase adds security CI gates |
| CCM-03  | Rollback plan              | ✅          | Git revert + Docker image tags    |

### DEV — Development Security (most relevant for code)

| Control | Requirement                | Demo Status | Gap / Mitigation                             |
| ------- | -------------------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| DEV-01  | Secure coding guidelines   | ✅          | `.claude/rules/code-style.md`                |
| DEV-02  | Input validation           | ✅          | Parameterised Cypher queries                 |
| DEV-03  | Output encoding            | 🟡          | React auto-escapes; CSP added D2             |
| DEV-04  | Authentication enforcement | ✅          | NextAuth + Keycloak OIDC                     |
| DEV-05  | Dependency management      | ✅          | `npm audit --audit-level=high` in CI         |
| DEV-06  | Static analysis            | 🟡          | ESLint + TypeScript strict; no SAST tool yet |
| DEV-07  | No hardcoded credentials   | ✅          | Env vars only; parameterised queries         |
| DEV-08  | Secrets scanning           | ⚠️          | No `detect-secrets` or `gitleaks` in CI yet  |
| DEV-09  | Security testing           | ✅          | SEC-01–SEC-10 E2E tests (D3)                 |
| DEV-10  | Vulnerability disclosure   | ⚠️          | No SECURITY.md or CVD policy yet             |

### IAM — Identity and Access Management

| Control | Requirement                  | Demo Status | Gap / Mitigation                                                                                                              |
| ------- | ---------------------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| IAM-01  | Authentication required      | ✅          | All routes (UI + API) require session; pentest D6 added getServerSession guards to all /api/admin/_ and /api/patient/_ routes |
| IAM-02  | Role-based access control    | ✅          | 7 Keycloak roles + middleware                                                                                                 |
| IAM-03  | Least privilege              | 🟡          | Role matrix implemented; no fine-grained ABAC                                                                                 |
| IAM-04  | MFA for privileged accounts  | ⚠️          | Keycloak MFA not configured in demo                                                                                           |
| IAM-05  | Session management           | ✅          | NextAuth sessions + NEXTAUTH_SECRET                                                                                           |
| IAM-06  | Credential lifecycle         | ⚠️          | Demo credentials are static                                                                                                   |
| IAM-07  | Privileged access management | ⚠️          | Admin role via Keycloak only; no PAM system                                                                                   |

### COS — Communication Security

| Control | Requirement                   | Demo Status            | Gap / Mitigation                                       |
| ------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| COS-01  | Encryption in transit         | ✅ (local) / 🔵 (prod) | HTTPS in production; HTTP localhost acceptable for dev |
| COS-02  | Strong TLS configuration      | ⚠️                     | Not validated; depends on reverse proxy                |
| COS-03  | Certificate management        | 🔵                     | Production only — cert rotation via Let's Encrypt      |
| COS-04  | Internal network segmentation | ⚠️                     | Docker network isolation only                          |

### DIP — Data Integrity and Protection

| Control | Requirement         | Demo Status | Gap / Mitigation                                  |
| ------- | ------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| DIP-01  | Data classification | ✅          | Threat model assets table                         |
| DIP-02  | Encryption at rest  | ⚠️          | Neo4j data not encrypted at rest in demo          |
| DIP-03  | Backup and recovery | ⚠️          | No backup for Neo4j volume in demo                |
| DIP-04  | Data minimisation   | ✅          | FHIR only returns requested fields                |
| DIP-05  | Audit logging       | ✅          | `TransferEvent` nodes, written by the neo4j-proxy |
| DIP-06  | Log integrity       | ⚠️          | Logs are mutable in Neo4j                         |

### LOG — Logging and Monitoring

| Control | Requirement            | Demo Status | Gap / Mitigation                       |
| ------- | ---------------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------- |
| LOG-01  | Security events logged | 🟡          | Access logs via Neo4j; no SIEM         |
| LOG-02  | Log retention          | ⚠️          | No retention policy; volume-based only |
| LOG-03  | Alerting on anomalies  | ❌          | No alerting in demo                    |
| LOG-04  | Log access control     | ⚠️          | Neo4j admin can modify logs            |

### INS — Incident Management

| Control | Requirement                      | Demo Status | Gap / Mitigation                       |

| INS-01  | Incident response plan           | ⚠️          | Not documented                         |
| INS-02  | Security incident classification | ⚠️          | Not defined                            |
| INS-03  | Breach notification process      | ⚠️          | GDPR Art. 33 requires 72h notification |

---

## Priority Gap Closure Plan

### Demo Phase (implement now)

| P0       | DEV-07  | Parameterised Cypher (D1)            | ✅ Done — Phase 23              |
| P0       | DEV-03  | CSP + security headers (D2)          | ✅ Done — Phase 23              |
| P0       | DEV-09  | Security E2E tests (D3)              | ✅ Done — Phase 23              |
| P0       | DEV-05  | npm audit in CI (D4)                 | ✅ Done — Phase 23              |
| P1       | DEV-08  | Add `detect-secrets` pre-commit hook | GitHub #4 — D5                  |

### Production Roadmap

| -------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| P0       | COS-01/02 | TLS 1.3 + HSTS + cert rotation                    |
| P0       | IAM-04    | MFA for EDC_ADMIN + HDAB_AUTHORITY                |
| P0       | DIP-02    | Neo4j disk encryption                             |

# Software bills of materials

One CycloneDX 1.5 file per deployable part, generated by
`scripts/security/generate-sbom.sh` (syft over the lockfiles, no `node_modules`
needed) and committed so a reviewer reads the bill next to the code it
describes. `--check` fails when a committed bill no longer matches the
lockfiles, which is how a dependency change that forgot the bill is caught.

| File                         | What                                      | Source of truth                                |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |

The iPhone app declares no third-party package, so its bill lists the Apple
frameworks it links (from the `import` statements, by
`scripts/security/generate-ios-sbom.py`) and says so in its metadata. That is
the checkable form of the claim in
[`docs/klarbefund/self-assessment.md`](/docs/security/klarbefund-self-assessment)
(BSI TR-03161 O.TrdP).

Vulnerabilities against these bills: `scripts/security/scan-repo.sh` runs
grype over them locally; `.github/workflows/security-scan.yml` does the same
in CI for the hub and uploads the result to the Security tab. Container
images are scanned separately, with trivy, in the same workflow.
